note: Complete Community Safety and Restoration System architecture — not isolated police or prison reforms. Not finished justice legislation. No invented crime, clearance, or recidivism statistics. Detailed statutes blocked until Phase 2.1 sourced diagnosis. Private-prison federal policy history is recorded accurately (2016 Yates phase-down; 2017 Sessions rescission; later executive orders may also change) to illustrate why durable principle should be settled in law.
role_in_philosophy: Justice is the mechanism that determines whether liberty, ownership, opportunity, and accountability are real—or merely promised. Community safety is a complete system: prevent harm, respond quickly, protect victims, treat addiction and mental illness, hold dangerous people securely, restore everyone who can be restored, and return as many people as safely possible to productive citizenship.

system_objective.text: Prevent harm, respond quickly when harm occurs, protect victims, treat addiction and mental illness, hold dangerous people securely, restore everyone who can be restored, and return as many people as safely possible to productive citizenship.
system_objective.not_merely: Neither merely softer nor merely tougher on crime.
system_objective.presence_rule: More visible human presence in communities, but fewer situations in which an armed officer is expected to function simultaneously as social worker, addiction specialist, mental-health clinician, school disciplinarian, homeless-services coordinator, traffic administrator, and criminal investigator.

community_safety_doctrine.text: Public safety belongs to the community. Police exercise authority on the community’s behalf, courts administer justice in the public trust, and correctional institutions exist to protect society and prepare people for responsible return whenever return is safely possible. No public-safety institution should profit from human confinement.

public_safety_promise.text: Every person should be protected from violence, exploitation, addiction, institutional abuse, and preventable disorder. Every victim should be supported. Every accused person should receive due process. Every dangerous person should be securely managed. Every person capable of restoration should receive a real path back. Every official exercising coercive authority should remain visible, reviewable, and accountable to the public.

community_policing_foundation.summary: Community policing rests on three recognized elements — community partnerships, problem-solving, and organizational transformation — that Constitutional Capitalism carries further by rebuilding the local safety system around permanent relationships and shared responsibility.

foundational_principle.text: Justice must protect the public, restrain wrongdoing, repair harm where possible, and return people to productive citizenship whenever safely achievable. It must never become a profit center, a political weapon, or a permanent system of social exclusion.

central_promise.text: A just society protects people from harm without surrendering the humanity of those who have caused harm. It holds wrongdoing accountable, repairs what can be repaired, and never converts punishment into permanent power over a person’s life.

central_questions.insufficient_alone: What punishment does this person deserve?
central_questions.required_also: What happened, who was harmed, what must be repaired, what protects the public, and what pathway returns the offender to responsible participation in society?

community_safety_corps.summary: Every community would operate a Community Safety Corps containing coordinated professions — broader than a traditional police department alone.

components.title: Sworn peace officers
responsibilities: traffic enforcement where danger is involved

components.title: Community officers
components.summary: Uniformed, highly visible personnel who may or may not possess full arrest powers, depending on role.

components.title: Behavioral-health response teams
components.summary: Clinicians and specially trained responders lead appropriate mental-health, suicide, substance-use, and nonviolent behavioral crises; police remain available when safety risks exist.

components.title: Community restoration officers
components.summary: Work with people who repeatedly encounter the justice system because of addiction, homelessness, unemployment, lack of identification, transportation problems, untreated illness, family instability, or reentry barriers — not to excuse misconduct, but to stop the cycle producing repeated public harm.

components.title: Victim-service officers
provides: help recovering documents, housing, employment, or property

recruitment_and_training.local_connection_rule: Local connection should be valued, but not used to protect old networks or exclude qualified outsiders.
officer_qualities: capable of both compassion and decisive action

relationship_policing.meaning: More police on the street means more relationships — not simply more stops or arrests.
relationship_policing.assigned_areas: Officers should have assigned community areas long enough to know families, businesses, schools, churches, recurring problems, leaders, vulnerable residents, and youth at risk.
relationship_policing.quota_ban: Arrest totals and citation numbers should never function as productivity quotas.

public_accountability_page_fields: disciplinary actions, with lawful privacy protections
transparency_and_review.body_camera_rule: Body cameras should support truth and accountability, but access rules must protect victims, children, private homes, medical crises, and people who were never charged.
anti_favoritism_safeguards: external review for deaths and serious force

public_corrections_rule.text: The state may not create a private financial interest in keeping human beings incarcerated.
public_corrections_rule.ban: No private prison, private jail, or private probation company should be paid according to occupied beds, length of confinement, supervision volume, or collected fees.
public_corrections_rule.federal_policy_instability_note: Federal private-prison policy has changed across administrations — e.g., the 2016 DOJ Yates memorandum sought to reduce privately operated federal prisons; the 2017 Sessions memorandum rescinded that directive. Later executive orders have also shifted federal contracting posture. A durable Constitutional Capitalism policy would settle the principle in law rather than leaving it to changing administrations.

decision_pathways.summary: Replace the jail pipeline with a quick assessment and correct pathway.

paths.title: Serious danger
responses: preparation for return when return becomes safe

paths.title: Addiction-driven conduct
responses: treatment courts and supervised recovery where evidence and circumstances support them
paths.evidence_note: Treatment courts combine judicial supervision with treatment, testing, sanctions, incentives, and transitional services; quality and outcomes depend heavily on program design.

paths.title: Mental-health crisis
responses: police involvement only in proportion to actual risk

paths.title: Poverty-related technical violations
paths.rule: A person should not be jailed simply because they cannot afford a fine, transportation, a class, supervision fees, electronic monitoring, or required treatment. Distinguish refusal from inability.

secure_restoration_campuses.summary: Prisons should be safe, humane, orderly, and productive — accountability without institutional abuse. Every incarcerated person receives an individualized plan; the daily schedule is built around responsibility.
secure_restoration_campuses.recidivism_note: Recidivism is a fundamental measure but must be defined carefully because rearrest, reconviction, and reincarceration capture different outcomes.

reentry_from_day_one.summary: Reentry should not begin a week before release. It is a continuum beginning with assessment and programming during confinement, followed by release planning, supervision, and community reintegration.
reentry_from_day_one.evidence_caution: Reentry-program evidence is not uniform; some evaluations find modest improvements in employment, housing, service access, and substance use. Demand rigorous evaluation rather than claiming every reentry service works.

productive_citizenship_destination.summary: After a sentence is completed, the person should have a defined pathway back into full civic and economic life. Restrictions should be tied to specific risks, not generalized lifetime exclusion.

restoration_councils.summary: Every county or regional community should have a Restoration Council monitoring system performance while protecting individual confidential case information.

core_commitments.title: Equal justice cannot depend on wealth
core_commitments.summary: Freedom and fundamental justice quality must not turn primarily on ability to pay bail, counsel, experts, fees, treatment, or court access.

core_commitments.title: Public safety remains essential
core_commitments.summary: Reform must not treat violence, exploitation, fraud, abuse, organized crime, or predatory conduct as harmless. Dangerous individuals may require secure confinement; victims deserve protection and voice; rehabilitation cannot sacrifice immediate public safety.

core_commitments.title: Punishment must be proportionate
core_commitments.summary: Punishment should not be grossly disconnected from harm, intent, role, future danger, and restoration possibility, nor exceed what is necessary to protect society, establish accountability, deter misconduct, and repair harm.

core_commitments.title: Justice should repair damage
core_commitments.summary: Restorative pathways (especially for nonviolent offenses with voluntary victim participation) expand the means of justice beyond imprisonment alone without replacing prosecution in every case.

core_commitments.title: Distinguish danger from dysfunction
core_commitments.summary: Addiction, mental illness, poverty, homelessness, trauma, and predatory disposition are not equivalent conditions; responses should match underlying cause while protecting the public.

core_commitments.title: No institutional profit from punishment
core_commitments.summary: No justice institution should have a financial incentive to arrest, charge, detain, supervise, fine, or incarcerate more people. Justice should be funded openly by the public.

core_commitments.title: Victims must not be forgotten
core_commitments.summary: Meaningful victim support includes safety, counseling, medical and economic recovery, restitution enforcement, notice, participation without controlling prosecution, and protection from retaliation.

core_commitments.title: White-collar and institutional wrongdoing with equal seriousness
core_commitments.summary: Accountability should reflect actual harm, including large-scale fraud, wage theft, environmental damage, corruption, and abuse of public trust.

core_commitments.title: Local authority with constitutional floors
core_commitments.summary: Communities should shape policing priorities, prevention, diversion, reentry, oversight, and public-safety budgeting; constitutional rights and minimum standards remain enforceable beyond local popularity.

core_commitments.title: Full reentry into citizenship
core_commitments.summary: After lawful sentence completion, punishment should not continue indefinitely through automatic lifetime exclusion; residual restrictions must be specific, relevant, reviewable, and limited.

stages.name: Prevention
stages.summary: Prevent harm before it occurs through human development, families, education, mental healthcare, addiction treatment, employment, transportation, housing, community institutions, and youth opportunity.

stages.name: Fair investigation and adjudication
stages.summary: Due process, timely proceedings, competent representation, evidence access, understandable charges, neutral decision-makers, protection from coercion, and independent review of police, prosecutors, defense, courts, labs, and corrections.

stages.name: Proportionate accountability
stages.summary: Sentencing considers harm, intent, prior conduct, danger, coercion, age, mental condition, rehabilitation potential, victim needs, and community safety; mandatory rules that erase meaningful differences receive close scrutiny.

stages.name: Rehabilitation and restoration
stages.summary: Sentences that can safely include return pathways should provide literacy, education, vocational training, behavioral healthcare, addiction treatment, financial education, family support, identification, employment preparation, and housing transition.

stages.name: Full reentry into citizenship
stages.summary: Clear rules for record sealing, licensing, employment, housing, voting, benefits, education, family rights, and credit access—with risk-specific exceptions that remain reviewable.

justice_test.title: Constitutional Capitalism Justice Test
justice_test.purpose: Screen every justice and community-safety policy before acceptance into the framework.

questions.text: Is the response proportionate to the harm?
Does wealth improperly determine the outcome?
Does any institution profit from punishment or confinement volume?
Does it use the least coercive professional response that still protects safety?
Is there a measurable path back to citizenship when return is safely possible?
Are officials accountable, transparent, and free from favoritism quotas?
Does the policy increase or reduce the long-term power and safety of ordinary people?

research_status.next: Phase 2.1: deepen COPS/BJA/NIJ/DOJ modules; attach justice baseline indicators; upgrade claims without inventing crime or recidivism statistics; keep Community Safety Corps as design agenda
